Each Executive Assistant will primarily support their assigned co-founder, while broader

Working Hours & Availability

These roles require working American hours, aligned with the assigned co-founder's U.S. time zone.

This is not a standard Monday-to-Friday, 9-to-5 position. You should be comfortable with:
- Non-standard or changing work hours when needed
- Occasional evening or weekend support
- Adjusting your schedule around travel, events, deadlines, and urgent priorities
- Being responsive when time-sensitive matters come up

Your regular working schedule, availability expectations, and any scheduling limitations will be discussed and agreed upon before starting.

Each assistant will primarily support their assigned co-founder. Broader

will be allocated between the two positions based on executive needs and individual strengths.

1. Executive Support
- Manage inboxes, calendars, task priorities, travel arrangements, and personal scheduling.
- Coordinate meetings across time zones, anticipate scheduling conflicts, and protect focus time.
- Prepare meeting briefs, presentations, agendas, follow-ups, and status updates.
- Monitor Slack communications, surface priority messages, and draft or send responses as authorized.
- Support HubSpot activity, CRM updates, and follow-ups on behalf of the assigned co-founder.
- Manage expenses, invoices, and administrative tasks requiring executive approval.
- Make calls and coordinate directly with internal and external contacts.
- Handle sensitive matters with confidentiality and discretion.

2. Event Planning
- Lead planning and execution for GrowthCon, our twice-yearly live event serving 200 to 400 loan officers.
- Coordinate venues, contracts, vendors, room blocks, travel, speakers, attendee communications, and branded materials.
- Manage event schedules, run-of-show documents, and event-day coordination.
- Partner with Sales and Marketing on promotion, registration, and the attendee experience.
- Support webinars, workshops, and other company events.
- Conduct post-event reviews and document improvements for future events.

3. Project Management
- Drive cross-functional initiatives and special projects from planning through completion.
- Maintain project dashboards, track deliverables, and follow up with internal teams.
- Identify blockers early and resolve or escalate them before they affect timelines.
- Coordinate leadership meetings, document decisions, assign action items, and track next steps.
- Support employee onboarding and offboarding across systems such as Asana, Slack, and HubSpot.
- Document and maintain standard operating procedures.

4. Cross-Team Communication
- Keep Sales, Marketing, and Operations aligned on leadership priorities.
- Draft internal communications, announcements, and updates.
- Monitor key Slack channels and ensure important information reaches the right people.
- Follow up on cross-functional commitments and maintain accountability.
- Represent the assigned co-founder's priorities in meetings when needed.

5. Content and Community Support
- Organize content and resources for our coaching community.
- Collaborate with Marketing and internal subject matter experts on editorial calendars and content delivery through Circle.so.
- Prepare presentations, reports, and written materials.
- Research industry trends, tools, and competitor activity.
- Support community engagement and ensure members receive timely attention and resources.

Tools & Systems

Experience with the following or similar platforms is not required but helpful:
- Asana
- Trello
- Slack
- HubSpot
- Circle.so
- Google Workspace or Microsoft Office
- Calendar and scheduling tools
- Project management and collaboration platforms

What Success Looks Like

You will be successful in this role if you can:
- Keep the assigned co-founder organized and focused on the highest-priority work.
- Anticipate needs instead of waiting to be told what to do.
- Take ownership of tasks and projects and follow them through to completion.
- Communicate clearly and professionally with internal and external contacts.
- Keep projects, events, meetings, and follow-ups organized even when priorities change.
- Make sound decisions within your level of authority and escalate appropriately when needed.
- Become a trusted partner who reduces the executive's administrative and operational workload.

Hiring Process

Candidates may be asked to complete a few practical exercises during the recruitment process, including:
- A live conversation or simulated phone call to assess communication skills
- A short writing exercise
- A prioritization scenario involving competing executive requests
- Questions about specific examples of taking initiative, solving problems independently, and managing multiple priorities

References from previous executive support roles may also be requested.
- Collaborative and supportive work environment.
- Stable, long-term remote work opportunity.
- Maxicare HMO after three months probationary period
